newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end marginally higher.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end marginally higher.

text.p: Australian shares ended marginally higher on Friday with options expiries dominating trade and market heavyweight BHP's annual profit well received by investors.

The All Ordinaries index was 2.5 points firmer at 2,702.4, but off its intra-day high of 2,709.0. Trade was strong with over A$2 billion (US$1.5 billion) worth of shares traded, although most of that was options-related activity.
Brokers said options trade masked any physical movement in stocks and it was no surprise the market ended reasonably flat, given the BHP result was in line with expectations.
BHP posted a 7.2-percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit to A$1.386 billion, close to the middle of analysts' forecast range of between A$1.35 billion and A$1.4 billion.
But the steel and resource giant's result included a near A$1 billion abnormal loss for asset write-downs across its businesses in steel, copper, petroleum and minerals.
Shares in BHP ended nine cents up at A$19.15, after falling to A$18.975, but were off their high of A$19.25.
"I think people were well pleased with the result, it was what they expected," said Richard George, funds manager with BNP Investment Management.

Brokers said it was hard to tell how much physical stock was traded in the overall volume because so much of it was options-related, adding that investors were also squaring their books ahead of the financial year closing date on Monday.
"It is very hard to read anything into it (today's market performance)," said Peter Morgan, head of equities at Perpetual Funds Management.
"We are in a period now where we have two days to go before the end of the financial year. You have got Wall Street a little bit weak and a lot of people around town have shut up shop," Morgan said.
